title: Preventing Self-Siphoning in P-Trap Installations
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering living spaces. A common issue during installation is creating a trap arm drop that exceeds the pipe's diameter before reaching the vent, effectively creating an S-trap. This setup causes self-siphoning: as water rushes out, atmospheric pressure drops, pulling the protective water seal out of the trap entirely. To maintain a functional seal, ensure the trap arm is pitched correctly and stays within the maximum unvented distance specified by your local code. Proper venting stabilizes pressure and protects the water seal.

Preventing Self-Siphoning in P-Trap Installations

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block dangerous sewer gases from entering living spaces. A common issue during installation is creating a trap arm drop that exceeds the pipe's diameter before reaching the vent, effectively creating an S-trap. This setup causes self-siphoning: as water rushes out, atmospheric pressure drops, pulling the protective water seal out of the trap entirely. To maintain a functional seal, ensure the trap arm is pitched correctly and stays within the maximum unvented distance specified by your local code. Proper venting stabilizes pressure and protects the water seal.
